samples.text:
The two plans show the ground floor of a museum in 1990 and at present. Overall, the museum today has more different facilities for visitors, such as a café and a gift shop, and the storage and offices have gone.

In 1990, visitors entered through the main entrance in the south into the entrance hall. Behind it was a ticket office. There was a local history gallery on the west and a natural history gallery on the east. In the north, there were a large painting gallery, a storage room and offices.

Today, the entrance hall and the local history gallery are same as before, but the ticket office has become an information desk. The natural history gallery was removed and a gift shop and a café is there now. The painting gallery is smaller than in 1990. The storage and the offices has been replaced by an interactive science zone, an education room and a area for temporary exhibitions. Also a lift has been added in the south-east.
samples.why: Overview present but basic · key changes all mentioned · basic sequencing and linking · adequate vocabulary · several errors in agreement, articles and word order, not affecting meaning.

samples.text:
The plans illustrate the layout of a museum's ground floor in 1990 and today. Overall, the museum has become more focused on visitor services and interactive learning, with storage and office space being converted into new exhibition areas.

In the southern half of the building, the main entrance and the entrance hall are unchanged, as is the local history gallery in the south-west. However, the ticket office in the centre has been replaced by an information desk, and the natural history gallery in the south-east has been removed. In its place, there are now a gift shop and, directly to its north, a café. A lift has also been installed in the south-east corner.

The northern half has undergone even more significant changes. The painting gallery in the north-west still exists but it has been reduced to about two-thirds of its former width. Next to it, an interactive science zone has been created, and the rooms previously used for storage and offices has been turned into an education room and a temporary exhibitions space.
samples.why: Clear overview · changes presented logically from south to north · good cohesive devices · some less common vocabulary · generally accurate with an agreement slip.

samples.text:
The plans compare the ground floor of a museum in 1990 with its current layout. Broadly speaking, back-of-house areas and one of the permanent galleries have made way for visitor facilities and more varied exhibition spaces, while the entrance area and the local history gallery have been retained.

On entering from the south, visitors still pass through the same entrance hall, beyond which the former ticket office now serves as an information desk. The local history gallery to the west is unchanged, but the natural history gallery that once occupied the south-eastern part of the floor has disappeared, its space now shared between a gift shop at the front and a café behind it. In addition, a lift has been installed in the south-eastern corner.

The northern side of the building has been reconfigured more extensively. The painting gallery, which previously stretched across nearly half the width of the floor, has been reduced in size, allowing an interactive science zone to be inserted beside it. The storage area and offices further east are no longer present, having been replaced by an education room and a space for temporary exhibitions.
samples.why: Precise overview of the shift in use · changes described in a clear spatial sequence · cohesion subtle and effective · wide, accurate vocabulary (back-of-house, reconfigured) · varied complex structures with no errors.
